2	name: project_handoff_delete_allow_installed_provider_override
3	description: "HANDOFF — the proper fix for provider mis-routing: delete allowInstalledProviderOverride so an explicit provider/model ref always beats the deployment-level defaultProvider. PR #2547 shipped the interim server-side patch; this is the end state, not started"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 92626692-978b-4702-9fbd-4012912a59f9

9	---
10	
11	**NOT STARTED.** Written 2026-08-06 as the handoff for the real fix. The interim
12	patch is MERGED (PR #2547, squash `1f0c004b9188e05ff9303d1a2530a48a2033b007`) and
13	stops the bleeding; this replaces it properly. Read
14	[[project_phantom_zai_provider_outranks_org_default]] first for the incident.
15	
16	## The design error, in one line
17	
18	`defaultProvider` is a **deployment-level** fact; the model ref is a **run-level**
19	fact. The worker routes by the deployment-level default and needs a permission
20	flag before a run-level ref may win. That precedence is backwards.
21	
22	## Why the flag exists and why the reason does not hold
23	
24	`agent-worker/src/runtime/model-resolver.ts` reroutes to a ref's own provider only
25	under `overrides.allowInstalledProviderOverride`, set from
26	`rawOptions.behaviorModelOverride` (`runtime/session-runner.ts:812`). The stated
27	justification is in the resolver's own comment: OpenRouter namespaces such as
28	`openai/gpt-4o` "must stay on OpenRouter even when standalone OpenAI is installed".
29	
30	That ambiguity is not reachable. Lobu stores refs as `<lobu-slug>/<model>`, so
31	OpenRouter's is `openrouter/openai/gpt-4o`. **Audited every `agents.models` ref on
32	prod 2026-08-06** — all nine prefixes are real Lobu provider slugs and the
33	OpenRouter entry keeps its prefix (`openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`):
34	
35	    prefix       refs  installed  example
36	    gemini          4  yes        gemini/gemini-2.5-flash
37	    qwen            4  yes        qwen/qwen3.8-max
38	    openrouter      4  yes        openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5
39	    z-ai            2  NO         z-ai/glm-5.2
40	    openai          2  yes        openai/gpt-4o-mini
41	    nvidia          1  NO         nvidia/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6
42	    deepseek-ai     1  NO         deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro
43	    deepseek        1  NO         deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
44	    xai             1  yes        xai/grok-4
45	
46	Re-run that audit before starting (query in the PR #2547 body). The flag also fails
47	to protect consistently: a per-Behavior override carrying the SAME ambiguous ref is
48	already permitted to reroute.
49	
50	## The fix
51	
52	1. **`agent-worker/src/runtime/model-resolver.ts`** — drop
53	   `allowInstalledProviderOverride` from the override branch's conditions. An
54	   explicit `<provider>/<model>` ref routes to that provider whenever
55	   `installedProviderRoutes[prefix]` exists. Keep that installed-route guard: it is
56	   what makes an uninstalled prefix (`z-ai`, `nvidia`, `deepseek*` above) fall
57	   through safely, exactly as today.
58	2. **`runtime/session-runner.ts:812`** — delete the mapping; then
59	   `allowInstalledProviderOverride` and `behaviorModelOverride` are both dead.
60	3. **`packages/server/src/gateway/services/platform-helpers.ts`** — delete the
61	   `isQualifiedModelRef(effectiveModelRef)` re-derivation block that #2547 added,
62	   and most of its 20-line comment. Keep `isQualifiedModelRef` — it still gates
63	   whether a per-request override is well-formed enough to win.
64	4. **Delete the caller-side assignments** now genuinely dead:
65	   `gateway/routes/public/agent.ts:1432`, `scheduled/jobs.ts:538`,
66	   `tools/admin/manage_conversations.ts:247`,
67	   `gateway/services/agent-threads.ts:192`. #2547 deliberately left these because
68	   removing them then would have regressed the working override path; once the flag
69	   is gone they are inert. Repo rule: remove, do not deprecate.
70	5. Tests to update: `packages/server/src/gateway/__tests__/platform-helpers-model-resolution.test.ts`
71	   (the `explicit model refs mark the routing override` describe block becomes
72	   obsolete) and `agent-worker` `model-resolver.test.ts` (50 tests, several assert
73	   the flag gates rerouting).
74	
75	**Blast radius is the reason #2547 shipped first**: this changes the server↔worker
76	dispatch contract and needs the worker image rebuilt and rolled out, not just two
77	server lines. Sequence it as its own PR.
78	
79	## Separate, independent defect — do NOT bundle
80	
81	`gateway/orchestration/deployment-manager.ts` ~line 2007: the `if (!primaryProvider)`
82	fallback scan accepts `candidate.hasSystemKey()`, so a deployment-wide key can make a
83	provider primary for an org that never configured it. That is very likely how `z-ai`
84	became `defaultProvider` for `buremba` — an org with no z-ai row, secret, or env key
85	of its own. Tenancy smell: a shared credential serving one org's traffic.
86	
87	Note the guard above it: `if (agentModel && effectiveProviders.length > 0 && …)`.
88	`findProviderForModel` (`gateway/auth/provider-catalog.ts:516`) WOULD have matched
89	`gemini/gemini-2.5-pro` — it falls back to matching the leading segment against
90	`providerId`, and its comment documents this exact mis-routing. So the fall-through
91	implies `agentModel` was empty at deployment time. **Unverified (~60%)** — confirm by
92	logging/observing before fixing.
93	
94	## Verification owed by whoever does this
95	
96	Reproduce the original signature first: an agent with `models: ["<provider>/<model>"]`,
97	NO per-Behavior `execution_config.model`, and a different `defaultProvider` — assert
98	the run routes to the agent's provider. That is the test #2547 could only express
99	through the flag. Then re-run the prod prefix audit above, and confirm buremba
100	Behaviors 5/20/70/71 still complete after their `execution_config.model` pins are
101	REMOVED (the pins are the workaround; the end state should not need them).
102	
103	Related: [[project_phantom_zai_provider_outranks_org_default]],
104	[[project_agent_model_provider_resolution]], [[feedback_put_the_check_at_the_chokepoint]].

3	description: "Agent-lane Behaviors resolved to a z-ai provider the org never configured (429 Insufficient balance), overriding the org's own default — worked around 2026-08-06 by pinning execution_config.model; ROOT CAUSE STILL UNKNOWN"

9	---
10	
11	Found 2026-08-06 while checking why org `buremba` was not healthy after the window-lag fix.
12	
13	## The symptom
14	
15	Agent-lane Behaviors failed at high rate with:
16	
17	    z.ai returned an error:
18	    429 Insufficient balance or no resource package. Please ...
19	
20	Behavior 5 (`Hourly Task Collaborator`): 39 failed / 10 completed over 3 days.
21	Behavior 71 (`Social interest radar`): 40 failed / 31 completed.
22	
23	**The user does not use z.ai at all.** Confirmed directly.
24	
25	## Why this is a real bug, not config drift
26	
27	Org `buremba` has NO z-ai anything:
28	- `inference_providers`: openai, gemini, **qwen (is_default = true)**. No z-ai row.
29	- `agent_secrets`: gemini-13, groq-14, openai-8/9, openrouter-7, qwen-19/20. No z-ai secret.
30	- agent `personal-agent` → `models: ["gemini/gemini-2.5-pro"]`.
31	- all four Behaviors had `execution_config = NULL` (no override).
32	- Neither `lobu-app` nor `lobu-worker` pod has `Z_AI_API_KEY` / `ZAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_*` set
33	  (checked names-only via `printenv | cut -d= -f1`).
34	
35	So nothing in the org's configuration selects z-ai, and the credential source is unaccounted for.
36	The only org with a z-ai secret is `atlas` (`z-ai-2`) — if that is being reached cross-org it is far
37	more serious than a quota error.
38	
39	## Where the label comes from
40	
41	`gateway/api/response-renderer.ts:196` → `labelProviderErrorBody(payload.error,
42	payload.errorContext?.provider)` → `utils/url-builder.ts:209` maps slug `z-ai` → display `z.ai`.
43	So the gateway genuinely resolved provider id **`z-ai`** for these requests.
44	
45	`auth/system-provider-resolution.ts` DOES prefer z-ai (`ZAI_PROVIDER_ID = "z-ai"`, chosen when
46	`hasClaudeSystemKey()` is false and `hasZaiSystemKey()` is true) — but its doc comment says it only
47	seeds `agents.models` **for freshly created agents**, and buremba's agent holds
48	`gemini/gemini-2.5-pro`, not a z-ai ref. So that file explains the PREFERENCE but not this
49	request-time resolution. **Chain not closed.**
50	
51	## The workaround (applied, verified)
52	
53	Pinning the Behavior's own model bypasses whatever picks z-ai:
54	
55	    client.behaviors.update({ behavior_id, execution_config: { model: "qwen/qwen3.8-max-preview" } })
56	
57	Applied to buremba 5, 20, 70, 71 on 2026-08-06 03:49 UTC. Verified in the DB, not from the SDK
58	response (`behaviors.get` returned an empty `execution_config` in the tool result — read the row).
59	
60	**Result: 4/4 triggered runs completed, 0 failures**, against prior base rates of 19% (Behavior 5)
61	and 41% (Behavior 71) — P(luck) ≈ 0.6%. Inference from outcome only: prod has **no per-call LLM
62	usage table** (`session_calls` does not exist; only `mcp_sessions` and `session`), and
63	`runs.model_used` records the literal string `lobu-agent`, so the provider actually used cannot be
64	observed directly. Runs took 18s and 31s.
65	
66	## Model-id gotchas
67	
68	- There is **no `qwen3.8-pro-preview`**. Verified against the live provider:
69	  `pi -p --no-session --model qwen/qwen3.8-pro-preview` → *"Model not found for provider qwen.
70	  Using custom model id"* (which would 404 upstream). The real tiers are `qwen3.8-max` and
71	  `qwen3.8-max-preview` (`config/providers.json`, added in #2532).
72	- The qwen catalog entry's `defaultModel` is **`qwen-max`**, NOT a 3.8 tier — so even with qwen as
73	  the org default, resolution lands on `qwen-max` unless a Behavior pins the 3.8 tier explicitly.
74	- `execution_config.model` is ONE field serving BOTH lanes: the device lane passes it as the CLI
75	  `--model` flag, the agent lane reads it via `getWatcherModelOverride`
76	  (`watchers/automation.ts:1156`). `pi --model qwen/qwen3.8-max-preview` works with no `--provider`
77	  flag — the provider rides in the ref, which matters because the Mac app's `pi` AgentSpec has
78	  `modelFlag: "--model"` and **no provider flag**.
79	
80	## Still owed
81	
82	- **Root cause**: why does an unconfigured system provider outrank an org's own default at request
83	  time? Affects every org, not just buremba.
84	- Orgs with an active qwen provider: buremba, community, atlas, lobu-team. **`emr-ekabakci` has
85	  openai only** — Behaviors 81/82/83 cannot use qwen until a qwen provider with the Token Plan
86	  upstream is added there.
87	- `community`'s Behaviors (2, 21, 22, 48, 52, 74) are unpinned and presumably hitting the same
88	  phantom z-ai.
89	
90	Related: [[project_behaviors_down_zai_quota]], [[project_agent_model_provider_resolution]],
91	[[reference_org_provider_needs_base_url]], [[project_behavior_window_cursor_lag]].

## Summary

- `defaultProvider` is a **deployment-level** fact; a `<provider>/<model>` ref is a **run-level** one. The worker routed by the deployment default and required a permission flag (`allowInstalledProviderOverride`, fed by `behaviorModelOverride`) before a ref was allowed to win. That precedence was backwards, and this deletes the flag: an explicit ref routes to its own provider whenever `installedProviderRoutes[prefix]` exists.
- #2547 (`1f0c004b`) was the interim server-side patch — it re-derived the flag from the ref that actually won so the gateway stopped dropping agent-level provider choices. This replaces it with the end state, so the flag, its mapping in `session-runner.ts`, the re-derivation block in `platform-helpers.ts`, and all four now-inert caller-side assignments are gone.
- **The installed-route guard stays** and is what keeps rerouting fail-safe: an uninstalled prefix (`z-ai`, `nvidia`, `deepseek*` on prod today) cannot conjure a provider the org never configured, and falls through exactly as before.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: `make test-unit` (exit 0), `make test-integration` (exit 0), targeted `bun test` on both resolver suites
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below

### Red → green

The reproducer is the prod signature: an agent pinned to `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro`, no per-Behavior override, and a `defaultProvider` of `z-ai` that the org never configured.

Before the fix (`packages/agent-worker/src/__tests__/model-resolver.test.ts`):

```

Expected: "gemini"
Received: "z-ai"

(fail) resolveModelRef > an agent-level ref routes to its own provider, not the deployment default

After:

```
packages/agent-worker/src/__tests__/model-resolver.test.ts:
packages/agent-worker/src/__tests__/model-resolver-harden.test.ts:

 0 fail
 162 expect() calls
```

### The prod A/B behind it

Org `buremba`, agent `personal-agent` pinned to `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro`, **no** z-ai provider row, secret, or system key anywhere in the org:

```
watcher_id  status     n   error
5           failed     39  z.ai returned an error: 429 Insufficient balance or no resource package
5           completed  10
71          failed     40  z.ai returned an error: 429 Insufficient balance or no resource package
71          completed  31
```

Setting a per-Behavior `execution_config.model` — the one thing that flipped the flag — fixed it: 4/4 runs completed against prior success rates of 19% and 41%.

## Notes

**Why the flag's stated justification does not hold.** The resolver's own comment said OpenRouter namespaces like `openai/gpt-4o` "must stay on OpenRouter even when standalone OpenAI is installed". Lobu stores refs as `<lobu-slug>/<model>`, so OpenRouter's are `openrouter/openai/gpt-4o` — the vendor namespace rides *inside* the ref and the prefix is never ambiguous. Re-audited every `agents.models` ref on prod 2026-08-06:

| prefix | refs | in an org where it is installed | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| gemini | 4 | 4 | `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash` |
| qwen | 4 | 4 | `qwen/qwen3.8-max` |
| openrouter | 4 | 1 | `openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` |
| z-ai | 2 | 0 | `z-ai/glm-5.2` |
| openai | 2 | 2 | `openai/gpt-4o-mini` |
| nvidia / deepseek-ai / deepseek | 1 each | 0 | — |
| xai | 1 | 1 | `xai/grok-4` |

Every stored prefix is a real Lobu provider slug, every OpenRouter ref keeps its `openrouter/` prefix, and **no org has OpenRouter as its default provider** — so the ambiguity the flag existed to protect against is not reachable from prod data. The flag also failed to protect consistently: a per-Behavior override carrying the *same* ambiguous ref was already permitted to reroute.

**Blast radius.** This changes the server↔worker dispatch contract, so the worker image must be rebuilt and rolled out — not just the server. `installedProviderRoutes`, `providerBaseUrlMappings`, and `credentialPlaceholders` are all built from the same `effectiveProviders` set in `gateway/index.ts`, so any provider that can now be a reroute target already has its proxy base URL published. A provider that is *installed* but has no usable credential now fails loudly with the existing "provider is not connected / no gateway routing URL" error instead of silently running on the fallback provider — which is the intended trade.

**Orgs whose routing changes on rollout** (agent `models[0]` prefix ≠ published default, prefix installed and `active`): `8dc12bdd…` → gemini, `UdNAH1…` → gemini, `org_lobucrm` → xai. All three provider rows are `active` with real key refs.

### Follow-ups, not in this PR

- `gateway/orchestration/deployment-manager.ts` `if (!primaryProvider)` accepts `candidate.hasSystemKey()` in its fallback scan, so a deployment-wide key can make a provider primary for an org that never configured it. That is very likely how `z-ai` became `defaultProvider` for `buremba`, and it is an independent defect.
- `buremba` Behaviors 5/20/70/71 still carry the `execution_config.model` pins added as the 2026-08-06 workaround. Once this is live they should be removed and the runs re-verified — the end state should not need them.

11	The exact sequence to get a `make task-setup` worktree testable in a browser. Verified 2026-07-29 in `.claude/worktrees/merge-snapshot-evidence` (PORT=9143). Each step below cost a wasted round-trip when skipped.
12	
13	**1. `make build` is a NO-OP — the target you want is `make build-packages`.**
14	`make build` prints "Nothing to be done for `build'" and exits 0, which looks like success. A fresh worktree has no `packages/*/dist`, so until you run `make build-packages` vitest dies at import time with `Failed to resolve entry for package "@lobu/pgvector-embedded"` and then `Failed to load url @lobu/core/contracts/interaction-envelope`. Both are the same missing-dist cause wearing different messages. Related: [[reference_worktree_stale_core_dist]], [[reference_empty_worktree_node_modules_resolves_main]].
15	
16	**2. `make dev` boots ONLY the API.** It runs `packages/server` (`tsx watch src/server.ts`) on the worktree's `.env.local` PORT. It does **not** serve the SPA — `/` and `/index.html` 404 (health reports `"mode":"cloud"`, and in cloud mode the frontend is hosted separately). `packages/owletto/dist/index.html` existing does not change this. Editing server TS is live via tsx watch; no restart needed.
17	
18	**3. The SPA is a second process — vite — and must use `LOBU_API_PROXY`, not `VITE_API_URL`.**
19	```
20	cd packages/owletto && LOBU_API_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<API_PORT> \
21	  bun run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port <pick a free one>
22	```
23	`prodApiProxy()` in `vite.config.ts` same-origin-proxies `/api`, `/oauth`, `/connect` and rewrites Set-Cookie (drops Domain, SameSite=None→Lax) so better-auth sessions work. `VITE_API_URL` does NOT work for auth — the config comments say so explicitly.
24	
25	**4. The SPA's backend is the ORIGIN. `/lobu` is the Agent API gateway only.**
26	Setting `VITE_API_URL=.../lobu` yields `GET /lobu/api/auth-config 404` and a "Not signed in" page. Measured on the live server:
27	```
28	/api/auth-config       -> 200
29	/lobu/api/auth-config  -> 404
30	```
31	See [[project_embedded_server_lobu_prefix]] — this is the same split, and it bites the SPA config too.
32	
33	**5. Dev DB is per-branch on 127.0.0.1:5418** (brew postgresql@18), named `lobu_<branch with / and - as _>` — e.g. branch `feat/merge-snapshot-evidence` → `lobu_feat_merge_snapshot_evidence`. Find it with `psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5418 -l`. A fresh one has 1 org (`local-install`), 1 user, 0 events — so an empty Activity page is EXPECTED, not a bug. Agents `lobu-builder` + `owletto-default` are seeded, but `inference_providers` is empty, so chat may not resolve a model (see [[reference_org_provider_needs_base_url]]).
34	
35	**6. Integration tests** want `lobu_test`, which is also reachable on 5418:
36	```
37	cd packages/server && DATABASE_URL="postgres://$USER@127.0.0.1:5418/lobu_test" PGSSLMODE=disable \
38	  node ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run <path> -t "<name>"
39	```
40	
41	**7. To exercise an AGENT-attributed tool call without wiring an LLM** — the useful trick, since the LLM only decides *to call* the tool and everything under test is downstream. Mint a PAT straight into the dev DB (`token = "owl_pat_" + randomBytes(24).toString("base64url")`, `token_hash = sha256(token)` hex, `token_prefix = token.slice(0,12)`, scope `'mcp:read mcp:write mcp:admin'`), then do the MCP streamable-HTTP handshake against `POST /mcp/<orgSlug>`:
42	`initialize` → read the `mcp-session-id` response header → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/call`. Send `x-lobu-agent-id: <agentId>` on every call. `classifyMutationPrincipal` gives `agentId` precedence over `userId`, so the context resolves to kind `"agent"` and takes the approval-gated branch instead of the human fast path. 43	
44	Do NOT sign in / create the local account yourself — that's the user's step.

fix(server): let an explicit model ref outrank the deployment default provider

`defaultProvider` is a deployment-level fact; a `<provider>/<model>` ref is a
run-level one. The worker routed by the deployment default and required a
permission flag (`allowInstalledProviderOverride`, fed by
`behaviorModelOverride`) before a ref was allowed to win. That precedence was
backwards: only the per-run dispatch sites set the flag, so a ref that was just
as explicit but arrived from `agent.models[0]` or the org default authorized
nothing and the run was silently re-pointed at whichever module the gateway's
credentialed fallback scan published.

`installedProviderRoutes[prefix]` exists. That installed-route guard stays and
is what keeps rerouting fail-safe: an uninstalled prefix cannot conjure a
provider the org never configured.

PR #2547 (`1f0c004b`) was the interim server-side patch that re-derived the flag
from the ref that actually won. This replaces it with the end state, so the
flag, its mapping in session-runner, the re-derivation block in
platform-helpers, and all four now-inert caller-side assignments are gone.

Learned 2026-08-06 doing the live A/B for PR #2554. Cost three full A/B rounds that
all produced a **false pass**.

## The trap

`make dev` runs `packages/server` under `tsx watch`, whose watch scope is
`packages/server` only. The embedded worker loads `@lobu/worker` **in-process at
server boot**. So:

- editing `packages/agent-worker/src/**` changes nothing in the running process;
- `cd packages/agent-worker && bun run build` (which DOES rewrite
  `dist/index.bundle.mjs`) also changes nothing — the module is already resolved;
- only a full dev-server restart picks the change up.

`packages/gateway/config/index.ts` prefers `src/index.ts` over
`dist/index.bundle.mjs` when `src/` exists, so reasoning "in-repo it runs source,
therefore my edit applies" is TRUE and still gives the wrong answer — the source was
read once, at boot.

## Why it reads as confirmation, not failure

Both arms of the A/B returned the SAME answer, and that answer was the one the
**pre-fix** arm was supposed to produce. A stale module does not error; it quietly
serves the old behavior to whichever arm you run. If the expected pre-fix result is
also what a stale post-fix run yields, three rounds look like clean corroboration.

**Detection that actually works:** add a temporary `logger.info("PROBE …")` to the
worker path under test and require it in the log before believing ANY arm. Its
absence is the only unambiguous signal that the code under test is not running.
Related: [[feedback_verify_the_mutation_applied]],
[[feedback_verify_dont_reason_from_construction]].

## Working loop

    edit packages/agent-worker/src/…
    pkill -TERM -f "worktrees/<slug>"      # kills ONLY this worktree's dev server
    make dev                                # wait for /api/health = 200
    <send request>                          # then read the probe line

Scope the `pkill` to the worktree path — a bare `pkill -f server.ts` also kills other
worktrees' dev servers (there were two live). See
[[feedback_concurrent_agent_worktree_wipe]].

  `POST /api/v1/agents/:id/messages` reaches `agentOptions.model`. Verify with
